items.title: Independent local failure with positive lower curvature
items.note: Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M41): "produces infinite full-BFGS runs, the same for every such pair" (before "produces the same infinite full-BFGS runs"): the runs do not depend on the pair, as in the quantifier order below. Quantifier order as in the TeX: ∃ F (strongly convex: EuclideanStrongConvexOn with κ > 0; compact sublevels; unique minimizer at 0; ¬DifferentiableAt F 0) and ∃ starts x₀ ℓ → 0, iterates x, matrices H with H ℓ 0 = I and limits x̄ ℓ, all before the pair; then ∀ admissible (c₁,c₂) ∃ runs R ℓ (AdmissibleBFGSRun: full BFGS with actual gradients) with exactly these iterates and matrices whose every line search is the implementation: NonStrictLineSearch.fromMetric F (x k) (H k) c₁ c₂ N = (some (α k), trialHistory (phase k)) for every trial budget N ≥ 5 (the non-strict search of failure.tex:22-35; it stops within five trials, so the budget plays no role: fromMetric_fuel_mono). Convergence to x̄ ℓ ≠ 0 with 0 ∉ ∂F(x̄ ℓ), x̄ ℓ → 0, F(x_k) strictly decreasing to F(x̄ ℓ) > F(0); the queries x + a(-Hg) for a ∈ trialHistory are the accepted and rejected queries (for every pair) and are differentiable; accepted lengths α(3m)=1, α(3m+1)=1/4, α(3m+2)=1/16; the supremum of the Euclidean query norms of run ℓ is finite (BddAbove) and its sSup tends to 0. Second paragraph: F = max of four branches f_i, each C¹ with globally Lipschitz (Euclidean) actual gradient and κ-strongly convex with one κ > 0; 0 < μ̲ ≤ L̄ with μ̲I ⪯ ∇²F(x) ⪯ L̄I (symmetric Hessian matrix RadialHessian.matrix F x = matrix of fderiv (fderiv F) x, quadratic-form bounds) at every x where F is differentiable nearby and fderiv F is differentiable at x (the convention of failure.tex:493-496); the first three branches have ¬DifferentiableAt (fderiv f_i) 0. Proof: the article package theorem LUniform.uniformSmoothLocalFailure (one orbit, objective and family of starts for every admissible pair; the whitened four-branch objective of Appendix art:lower_curvature), plus the per-run boundedness of queries from their convergence.
